title: Kunsthaus Zürich: Masterpieces
subtitle: Twenty works that distribute attention through colour, intervals and the pressure of bodies.
introduction:
Mondrian’s red square and Hodler’s broad lake ask a related question in very different forms: how much can a large area of colour do? One painting dispenses with a depicted place; the other remains a view of Lake Geneva. Their resemblance is a useful comparison, not evidence that landscape must develop into abstraction.

The other works complicate the question. A caught trout is held close to the surface, a scholar pauses over his book, and archaeologists work beneath a church arch. Shape and spacing are never merely decorative decisions. They determine what sort of access the spectator has to a person, a place or an event.
visitNote: The twenty paintings are selected collection works, not a guaranteed route through the Kunsthaus buildings. Check individual records for current location, loans and display changes before visiting.

books.title: Concerning the Spiritual in Art
books.author: Wassily Kandinsky; translated by Michael Sadleir
books.note: Kandinsky’s writing gives a contemporary argument for the independence of colour and form. Read it beside Itten and Mondrian, then return to Hodler’s recognizable landscapes to see where the comparison remains useful and where it stops.

works.title: Composition with Red, Blue and Yellow
works.catalogueTitle: Composition with Red,  Blue and Yellow
works.credit: Piet Mondrian. Composition with Red,  Blue and Yellow. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/piet-mondrian/composition-with-red-blue-and-yellow-1930
works.description: The red area dominates without occupying the centre of a symmetrical design. Smaller blue and yellow sections act across unequal intervals of white, held apart by black lines. With no depicted object to identify, attention falls on those differences themselves: the weight of one area depends on what has been left beside it.

works.title: The Gardener
works.credit: Gardener. WikiArt; Georges Seurat. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.description: The long tool’s diagonal gives the gardener’s stance a clear purpose. Broad marks allow the surrounding growth to remain less individually described than the man and his work. This is a useful place to resist expecting a familiar later Seurat technique: the painting’s immediate structure comes from a body, a tool and a patch of ground.

works.title: Lake Geneva from Caux
works.credit: Ferdinand Hodler. Lake Geneva from the Caux. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/ferdinand-hodler/lake-geneva-from-the-caux-1917
works.description: The lake occupies the view as a broad turquoise shape before small details of place become important. Its curve is distinct from the mountains and cloud band beyond. Hodler does not abandon geography, but concentrates its recognition into a few boundaries; an extensive distance is made readable through a compact arrangement of colour.

works.title: Lake Geneva in the Evening from Chexbres
works.catalogueTitle: Lake Geneva on the evening in Chexbres
works.credit: Ferdinand Hodler. Lake Geneva on the evening in Chexbres. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/ferdinand-hodler/lake-geneva-on-the-evening-in-chexbres-1895
works.description: Bare trees interrupt the bands of water and evening sky. They establish a near position from which the more distant light can be seen, preventing the stripes of colour from becoming entirely detached from a place. Compare this with the later Caux view, where the lake’s large shape carries more of the composition.

works.title: Landscape at Caux with Rising Clouds
works.catalogueTitle: Landscape at Caux with increasing clouds
works.credit: Ferdinand Hodler. Landscape at Caux with increasing clouds. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/ferdinand-hodler/landscape-at-caux-with-increasing-clouds-1917
works.description: Clouds rise above the lake in broken forms that answer the curved foreground without copying it. The resemblance gives the scene coherence while preserving the difference between solid terrain and changing vapour. Alongside the other Hodlers, this is an opportunity to follow one painter adjusting relationships within a recurring landscape subject.

works.title: Johann Joachim Winckelmann
works.credit: Angelica Kauffman. Portrait of Johann Joachim Winckelmann. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/angelica-kauffman/portrait-of-johann-joachim-winckelmann-1764
works.description: Winckelmann’s pen remains above the book, but his head turns away from the page. Writing has been interrupted rather than completed or abandoned. That small discrepancy makes the portrait active: the scholar’s occupation is identifiable, while his attention reaches beyond the immediate task represented by the objects in front of him.

works.title: Pierre Loti
works.credit: Henri Rousseau. Portrait of Pierre Loti. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/henri-rousseau/portrait-of-pierre-loti
works.description: The fez, cat, tree and distant industrial forms are kept distinct rather than absorbed into a continuous naturalistic setting. Their unequal scales make the image feel assembled. The sitter’s identity is presented through a combination of signs, so that recognition depends on the arrangement as much as on a convincing account of shared space.

works.title: Sleeping Venus Surprised by a Satyr
works.credit: Nicolas Poussin. Sleeping Venus, surprised by Satyr. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/nicolas-poussin/sleeping-venus-surprised-by-satyr-1626
works.description: The sleeping figure and the approaching satyr do not share the same awareness of the encounter. Poussin establishes that inequality through their contrasting bodily states: rest against movement, exposure against active looking. The mythological subject does not remove the tension. It gives that imbalance a narrative setting.

works.title: The Apostle Simon
works.credit: The Apostle Simon. WikiArt; Rembrandt van Rijn. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.description: Before identifying an apostle, the picture offers an ageing face and hands brought forward by limited light. The dark object held close to the chest belongs to that concentrated bodily presence. Sacred identity is not staged through a broad public scene; it is encountered at the scale of one person.

works.title: The Meeting
works.credit: Johannes Itten. The Meeting. WikiArt source label: Public domain US. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/johannes-itten/die-begegnung-1916
works.description: A turning circular arrangement meets a dark upright form. The title encourages an idea of encounter, but there is no need to translate each shape into a person. Their differing directions already establish a relation: one suggests rotation, another holds its position, and the coloured bands make the intersection visible.

works.title: The Servant
works.credit: Amedeo Modigliani. The Servant. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/amedeo-modigliani/the-servant-1916
works.description: The slight inclination of the head prevents the frontal pose from becoming rigid. A long neck and sloping shoulders carry the sitter’s presence through a small number of curves, while rougher colour surrounds her. The portrait is economical, but its economy concentrates attention on posture rather than making the woman interchangeable.

works.title: The Trout
works.credit: The Trout. WikiArt; Gustave Courbet. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.description: The trout’s open mouth and bent body occupy the near foreground with little surrounding distraction. Its spotted skin is an identifying surface, but the picture also insists on the animal’s physical weight. This is a catch shown as a body, not an abundance of food arranged at a comfortable distance.

works.title: Vanity
works.credit: Giovanni Segantini. Vanity. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/giovanni-segantini/vanity-1897
works.description: The woman bends toward a pool, a familiar situation of looking that the dark form in the water complicates. Pale animals and green slopes remain comparatively readable around her. The uncertainty is localised: it gathers where a reflection might be expected, preventing the pastoral setting from settling into uncomplicated reassurance.

works.title: Houses of Parliament, Sunset
works.credit: Claude Monet. Houses of Parliament, Sunset. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The buildings remain recognisable while their edges are partly lost in orange-red haze. That limited recognition matters: without it, the changes of light would have no stable subject against which to register. Reflections carry the colour into the water, where architecture becomes still less solid than it is above.

works.title: My Models
works.credit: Giovanni Segantini. My Models. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/giovanni-segantini/meine-modelle-1888
works.description: An easel, figures and a painted scene share the studio, making it necessary to distinguish objects from their representations. The room is occupied by both models and the work made from them. Rather than hiding the conditions of production, Segantini makes those conditions part of what the painting asks the spectator to sort out.

works.title: War
works.credit: Arnold Böcklin. War. Image credit: Arnold Böcklin; Source credit: The Yorck Project (2002) 10.000 Meisterwerke der Malerei (DVD-ROM), distributed by DIRECTMEDIA Publishing GmbH. ISBN : 3936122202 .. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: Horses’ limbs, raised arms and falling bodies collide in a space that leaves little separation between one action and the next. The title names a condition rather than a documented battle. Böcklin gives it bodily consequences: the compression makes destructive movement clearer than any secure position from which to watch it.

works.title: Bodmer and Fuseli before the Bust of Homer
works.catalogueTitle: Bodmer und Füssli vor der Büste Homers
works.credit: Henry Fuseli. Bodmer und Füssli vor der Büste Homers. Image credit: Henry Fuseli. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The bust’s size prevents Homer from remaining a small decorative reference behind a conversation. It shares the space emphatically with the two men and the gesture between them. An inherited literary authority thus takes a material form: something present enough to organise how the living figures sit and address one another.

works.title: Adoration of the Magi
works.credit: Hans Fries. Anbetung der Heiligen Drei Könige. Image credit: Hans Fries; Source credit: Kunsthaus Zürich. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: Costume, gifts and faces crowd into the panel around Mary and the child. The material density makes the act of approach tangible: each visitor has a position and something to bring, even where bodies overlap. Devotion is expressed through an encounter among differently dressed people rather than through empty space around an isolated figure.

works.title: Archaeologists in the Church of Valeria
works.catalogueTitle: Archäologe in der Kirche von Valeria
works.credit: Rafael Ritz. Archäologe in der Kirche von Valeria. Image credit: Rafael Ritz; Source credit: Kunsthaus Zürich. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The church interior is being examined, not simply admired from an unoccupied viewpoint. Equipment and small investigators give historical study a place within the building’s fabric. The large arch makes their relative size apparent, holding individual acts of inspection inside a structure that exceeds what any one figure can take in.

works.title: Evening Landscape with a Flock of Sheep
works.credit: Robert Zünd. Abendlandschaft mit Schafherde. Image credit: Robert Zünd; Source credit: Kunsthaus Zürich. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The moving flock provides a route from the shaded foreground toward the pale distance. Tall trees contain the near space, while the opening beyond permits it to continue. The scene’s repose is therefore organised rather than motionless: light and passage give the sheep somewhere to go.

closingSections.title: Keep the comparisons local
paragraphs: The three Hodlers make one compact group; Mondrian and Itten make another. Compare the actual intervals and directions before reaching for a movement label. These works form a collection selection, not a guaranteed gallery route. Consult the Kunsthaus for current displays and access.
